angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 1,294,002 km at 288.94 pc = 0.06 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 3.4609 +/- 0.0118 mas (same row, RUWE 0.91): 288.94 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.86 +/- 0.19 solar radii from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-63 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract): 1,294,002 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.28 +/- 0.42 solar masses from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-63 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5550 +/- 100 K from Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-63 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Stassun et al. 2017, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-63 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-63.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.006, rounded to two decimals
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-63 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.08 dex, from Stassun et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017AJ....153..136S/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-63 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.44936, from Gaia DR2 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2018A&A...616A...1G/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-63 (pscomppars): age 8.3 Gyr, from Bonomo et al. 2017 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2017A&A...602A.107B/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: VizieR J/ApJ/919/138/table1 (Rot. vel. & per. of hot Jupiter host stars), column Prot: 37 d, the row 0.0 arcsec from the star's J2000 place
